t: Khoe and San peoples lived on the Cape peninsula and traded with passing ships long before the Dutch East India Company landed in 1652 and began a permanent settlement.
The Dutch and then the British ruled the city, which depended on enslaved labour until the 1830s and drew on people brought from Asia and Africa, and it passed to Britain permanently in 1814.
Under apartheid whole communities were removed, most notably the more than 60,000 residents of District Six, and the city remains one of the most racially segregated in South Africa.
dyk: In 1510 the Portuguese admiral Francisco de Almeida and sixty-four of his men were killed at the Battle of Salt River by the Goringhaiqua, who used cattle trained to respond to whistles and shouts.
ev: Bartolomeu Dias reaches the Cape and names it the Cape of Storms
The Goringhaiqua defeat a Portuguese force at the Battle of Salt River
Jan van Riebeeck lands with employees of the Dutch East India Company to found a permanent station
A first large group of 402 enslaved people is brought to the Cape
British forces take the Cape after the Battle of Blaauwberg
District Six is declared a white-only area and its housing is demolished
Nelson Mandela speaks from the balcony of the City Hall hours after his release
The first democratic election is held on 27 April

f.founded: Jan van Riebeeck and other employees of the Dutch East India Company landed on 6 April 1652 to establish a permanent station at the Cape; Khoe and San peoples had lived in the region long before.
f.where: On the shore of Table Bay, at the foot of Table Mountain, on the Cape Peninsula in the Western Cape of South Africa.
f.known: The Khoe and San peoples of the Cape; the Dutch East India Company's station of 1652; the Castle of Good Hope; slavery and its end; the Cape Qualified Franchise; District Six and the forced removals of apartheid; Robben Island; Nelson Mandela's first public speech after his release
f.today: Cape Town is the legislative capital of South Africa, the seat of its Parliament, and the capital of the Western Cape.
